note: Lach Truong (76), tirage de juin 1943. Three edges are printed and were read off the scan by eye at full resolution: 115g,00 horizontally at NW, 22g,12'5" vertically at NW and NE, 22g,00 at SE. NOTHING is printed at either east corner, and the reason is that there is no graticule value there to print: 76 is the survey's eastern edge sheet at the coast -- its own printed index diagram shows empty cells east of it -- so the sheet was cut where the mapping stopped rather than on a meridian. East is therefore derived from the detected quad, and it is not a free parameter: of the candidate spans 0.10 / 0.1125 / 0.125 / 0.1375 / 0.140 / 0.15 / 0.1875 / 0.20 grades, 0.1375 puts the two ground scales 0.25% apart and the next best is 1.57%. Corners come from the detector, not from a person: the frame fits on three sides at 0.46-0.74 px residual and salvage_side recovers the fourth at 82.9 px against the others' 84.8/84.8/84.1.
